rows.subtopic: Recovering from a major work mistake
rows.subtype: Approach: adding a checklist and guardrail [Action]
rows.description: The team adds a required review for destructive commands, separates test and production credentials and writes a short checklist, so the same slip cannot repeat.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, contingency planning, seeking advice

rows.subtopic: Recovering from a major work mistake
rows.description: The employee replays the error for days and starts doubting every task, becoming slower and more error-prone, which shows how shame can damage performance as much as carelessness.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, checklist, contingency planning, seeking advice

rows.subtopic: Recovering from a major work mistake
rows.subtype: Approach: apologising and offering repair to the client [Action]
rows.description: The manager and employee call the affected client, explain the issue plainly, share recovery timelines and offer a service credit, which rebuilds credibility better than excuses.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, checklist, contingency planning, seeking advice

rows.subtopic: Recovering from a major work mistake
rows.subtype: Approach: putting the event in perspective with a mentor [Thinking]
rows.description: A senior colleague shares a similar mistake from earlier years and how it was handled. The employee sees the error as fixable and learns that recovery matters more than perfection.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, checklist, contingency planning

rows.subtopic: Recovering from a major work mistake
rows.subtype: Approach: rebuilding trust with small reliable deliveries [Revision]
rows.description: Over the next months, the employee delivers tasks on time, communicates delays early and keeps the team informed, and gradually regains bigger responsibilities.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, checklist, contingency planning, seeking advice

rows.subtopic: Recovering from a major work mistake
rows.subtype: Approach: sharing lessons with the wider team [Revision]
rows.description: The employee presents a short talk on what failed and what changed. Others start reporting near misses, showing that openness can make the whole team safer.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: avoidance and procrastination, checklist, contingency planning, seeking advice

rows.subtype: Approach: working backward from a target role [Thinking]
rows.description: A developer aiming to become an architect by twenty-nine lists what that role needs, such as system design, leading a team and domain depth, then assigns each to a year.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning, experiment and measure, rigid persistence, seeking advice, values-first planning

rows.subtype: Approach: yearly themes with quarterly goals [Action]
rows.description: Year one focuses on core skills, year two on ownership of a module, and so on. Each quarter has one or two measurable goals, reviewed in a short written note.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning, experiment and measure, rigid persistence, seeking advice, values-first planning, working backward

rows.subtype: Approach: following the highest salary each time [Pitfall]
rows.description: The person hops to whichever company pays most, ignoring learning and reputation. After four years the resume shows many names but little depth or a clear direction.
graph_context: same problem, other approaches: adaptive replanning, experiment and measure, rigid persistence, seeking advice, values-first planning, working backward

rows.subtype: Approach: keeping options open through broad skills [Thinking]
rows.description: Uncertain about the future, the person builds transferable skills such as communication, data handling and cloud basics, accepting that specialisation may come later once interests clarify.
